summary: The Shop is 33 members held together by a real, working anatomy — Charter / Voice / Tiers / Job Contract / Self-Check / Gotchas / Recipes — and it's the most internally consistent family I've read in the palace: every alive `specialist` declares `directed-by [[Maker]]`, every one declares `member-of [[The Shop]]` (so Maker's generated Roster table has one source of truth, not three), and the "earn your entry by a genuinely different operating model" bar is enforced for real in each entry's Lost Branches section — that's why nothing here wants merging or composting despite Loudon's "good but cluttered" read this morning. The clutter, where it's real, isn't duplicate entries; it's two smaller things: one broken convention (LoRA Trainer is missing the `directed-by Maker` link every sibling carries, which is also why it and OBS sit at zero inbound — they're newcomers the rest of the family hasn't reached back to yet), and one un-closed pattern — six different specialists (Matplotlib, LaTeX, Mermaid, ffmpeg, Tone.js, Web Audio Worklet) independently ask "should the Shop build a house-defaults wrapper for me?" as if it were a fresh question, when Maker's own Articulated Cascade section already answered it in general (Observable Plot's `palacePlot()` wrapper is the proof it works) — the rule exists, it just hasn't been executed six more times. The one genuine architectural signal worth Loudon's attention: Maker's own Open Questions set a threshold ("when the Roster grows past ~15 specialists, Selection Heuristics gets unwieldy") and the roster is now at 33, more than double that line, with OBS independently naming itself "a second push on the same wall" toward a Producer layer above the Maker — two members of the family are now flagging the same seam from different directions.

typed_relations.label: capture-to-batch
typed_relations.evidence: OBS Recipes: 'Tail without re-encoding. Hold an end-card scene for a beat before stopping the recording... The video stream is then copied, never re-encoded' — a batch/finishing move that is ffmpeg's own charter. OBS already declares the reciprocal link (ffmpeg couples-with, label capture-to-batch) but ffmpeg does not declare it back.
typed_relations.rationale: OBS has zero inbound and is a flagged newcomer/unreachable entry; ffmpeg is explicitly 'the meeting place where any two Specialists' outputs come together,' and OBS's own Recipes section names ffmpeg's exact role. Reciprocating the symmetric couples-with link is a genuine, not forced, fix.

typed_relations.label: trains-loras-here
typed_relations.evidence: RunPod GPU Backend Untested Horizons: 'LoRAs / fine-tunes — style packs or alternate checkpoints, loaded on a pod.' LoRA Trainer's own frontmatter already declares rides-the-substrate back to RunPod GPU Backend, but the substrate doesn't point back.
typed_relations.rationale: LoRA Trainer is a flagged newcomer with 0 inbound; RunPod GPU Backend literally names LoRA training as an open horizon of its own substrate. The two entries are already talking about each other in prose; only the frontmatter link is missing on one side.

typed_relations.label: agent-namespace-by-worktree
typed_relations.evidence: RunPod GPU Backend Gotchas: 'a single-sourced per-agent slug at `_ops/runpod/agent_ns.py` ($RUNPOD_AGENT_SLUG → git worktree name → host)' — the fix for the multi-agent pod-collision outage reads the git worktree name directly to derive the pod namespace.
typed_relations.rationale: This is a structural, not thematic, tie: the actual mechanism that prevents two agents' RunPod pods from colliding is keyed on the git worktree identity. I have not read Worktree Practice itself, so I can't confirm the target's own framing matches — flagging as a bridge candidate for an elder to verify rather than a settled find.
typed_relations.deep_pattern: Both are instances of 'give the concurrent-agent a durable, structural name instead of a shared default' — the same move assume-multi-agent generalizes, applied at the git layer instead of the account layer.
typed_relations.fidelity_test: unverified — I did not read Worktree Practice.md; propose, don't assert.

entry_health_flags.graffiti_note: Every other alive specialist in this family declares `{ target: "[[Maker]]", type: connects-to, label: directed-by }`. LoRA Trainer is the one exception — its links list (RunPod GPU Backend, The Shop, BLUELINE — Production Plan, Capability-first prototyping, Review Layer) never names Maker at all, even though Maker's Promotion Log narrates its origin. Propose adding the standard directed-by link to bring it into the family's own convention.

coherence_findings.issue: Six specialists independently carry the same unresolved Open Question — 'should the Shop build a house-defaults wrapper for me?' — as if it were novel, when Maker's own Articulated Cascade § 'Layer 0 — the tool's own taste' already states the general rule (build the skin wrapper before the second styled job) and Observable Plot's palace-plot-defaults.js is the proof it works.
coherence_findings.proposed_action: Each entry's own Open Questions should be updated to point at Maker § Articulated Cascade (Layer 0) as the already-decided policy, converting 'should we?' into 'when does this one earn its wrapper' — a smaller, sharper question. Not a merge; a citation fix across six entries.

coherence_findings.issue: Maker's own Open Questions set a numeric threshold for when the Selection Heuristics section (and implicitly the flat single-Maker architecture) gets unwieldy — 'when the Roster grows past ~15 specialists.' The Roster is now 33, more than double that line, and a second, independent member of the family (OBS) has separately flagged the same seam from the opposite direction ('I am the second independent pressure on the Shop's Producer-layer seam... two pushes on one wall is the kind of thing that should move the architecture').
coherence_findings.proposed_action: Not mine to resolve at folder-lens — flagging for Loudon/an elder as a should-act item: two independent stress signals (roster size, real-time-with-a-human operating model) both point at the same missing layer above the Maker.

coherence_findings.proposed_action: Not urgent — Hero and Avatar Maker's own stated priority order (projects, then philosophies, then most-connected hubs) doesn't cover Shop specialists explicitly, so this isn't a broken promise, just an inconsistency worth a note if a future face-batch reaches the Shop.
